subject: psychology
topicDisplay: Option 1 Relationships Gender Cognition And Development
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: The episodic buffer was added to the working memory model in 2000 to do what?
options: Integrate information from the subsystems and link to LTM
questions.explain: Baddeley added the episodic buffer to integrate visual, spatial and verbal information and link working memory to LTM.

questions.q: Interference is most likely to cause forgetting when the two sets of information are what?
questions.explain: Interference effects are strongest when the competing memories are similar, as McGeoch and McDonald showed.

questions.q: According to Rusbult, commitment (rather than satisfaction) explains why some people:
options: Stay in unsatisfying or abusive relationships
questions.explain: Because commitment includes investment, partners may stay even when dissatisfied, as leaving would mean losing what they invested.

questions.q: Memory for how to perform skills such as riding a bike is which type of LTM?
questions.explain: Procedural memory stores motor skills and actions performed largely without conscious effort.

questions.q: Social exchange theory describes relationships in terms of:
options: Rewards minus costs producing a profit or loss
Equal inputs and outputs for both partners
questions.explain: Thibaut and Kelley's social exchange theory views relationships as an economic exchange where people seek to maximise rewards and minimise costs.

questions.q: In the BSRI, an individual scoring low on both masculinity and femininity is classified as:
questions.explain: Bem's typology classifies those low on both dimensions as 'undifferentiated', distinct from androgynous (high on both).

questions.q: The 'halo effect' in attraction refers to the assumption that physically attractive people:
options: Also possess other desirable personality traits
questions.explain: The halo effect (a physical attractiveness stereotype) leads us to assume attractive people also have positive traits like kindness.

questions.q: In Loftus and Palmer's study, changing the verb in 'how fast were the cars going when they ___ each other?' affected what?
questions.explain: Leading verbs like 'smashed' produced higher speed estimates than 'contacted', showing misleading information affects EWT.

questions.q: The case of patient KF, who had poor verbal STM but intact visual STM, challenged the MSM by suggesting what?
options: STM is a single unitary store
Coding in STM is always semantic
STM has multiple components, as in the working memory model
questions.explain: KF's selective deficit suggests STM is not unitary, supporting the multiple components of the working memory model.

questions.q: The intra-psychic phase of Duck's model is characterised by:
options: Privately weighing up the partner's faults and dissatisfaction
Joint discussions to repair the relationship
questions.explain: The intra-psychic phase involves one partner's private dissatisfaction and brooding before anything is voiced.

questions.q: Which hormone is most associated with the development of male genitalia and masculinising the brain prenatally?
questions.explain: Testosterone drives the development of male sex organs and is implicated in masculinising aspects of the developing brain.

questions.q: What is the widely accepted capacity of short-term memory according to Miller?
questions.explain: Miller's 'magic number' suggests STM holds about 7 plus or minus 2 items or chunks.

questions.q: The cognitive interview was developed by Fisher and Geiselman to do what?
options: Improve the accuracy and amount of recall from eyewitnesses
questions.explain: The cognitive interview uses psychological techniques to enhance the quantity and accuracy of eyewitness recall.

questions.q: In social exchange theory, the comparison level (CL) refers to:
options: The point at which a relationship ends
The standard of rewards we believe we deserve, based on past experience
The rewards available in alternative relationships
questions.explain: The comparison level is the expected standard of rewards judged against previous relationships and social norms.

questions.q: Androgyny, as measured by the Bem Sex Role Inventory (BSRI), refers to:
options: An absence of both masculine and feminine traits
A high level of both masculine and feminine traits
questions.explain: Androgyny is a balance of high masculine AND high feminine traits; the BSRI measures these on independent scales.

questions.q: Klinefelter's syndrome is characterised by which chromosome pattern?
questions.explain: Klinefelter's syndrome affects biological males who have an additional X chromosome (XXY).

questions.q: The correct sequence of Kohlberg's stages of gender development is:
options: Gender constancy, gender stability, gender identity
Gender stability, gender identity, gender constancy
Gender identity, gender stability, gender constancy
Gender schema, gender identity, gender constancy
questions.explain: Kohlberg proposed gender identity (~2), gender stability (~4), then gender constancy (~6).

questions.q: The case of David Reimer is often cited as evidence that:
options: Hormones play no role in gender
Gender is entirely determined by upbringing
Biological sex is difficult to override through socialisation alone
questions.explain: David Reimer, raised as a girl after a circumcision accident, never identified as female — suggesting biology constrains gender identity.

questions.q: According to filter theory, complementarity becomes the most important factor:
questions.explain: Kerckhoff and Davis found complementarity (meeting each other's needs) matters most in longer-term relationships, after similarity of values.

questions.q: In the working memory model, the phonological loop deals with which type of information?
questions.explain: The phonological loop processes auditory and speech-based (verbal) information.

questions.q: Proactive interference occurs when what happens?
options: New information disrupts recall of older information
Older information disrupts recall of newer information
Information decays in the sensory register
questions.explain: In proactive interference, previously learned information disrupts the recall of more recently learned information.

questions.q: The cognitive interview technique of recalling events in a different order helps because it does what?
options: Reduces the influence of prior expectations or schema on recall
questions.explain: Changing the recall order disrupts schema-driven expectations, reducing reconstructed or dishonest reporting.

questions.q: In equity theory, a partner who feels under-benefited is likely to experience:
options: Dissatisfaction, often with anger or resentment
questions.explain: Under-benefited partners typically feel anger and resentment, whereas over-benefited partners may feel guilt — both reflect inequity.

questions.q: Social learning theory explains gender development primarily through:
options: Modelling, imitation and differential reinforcement of gender-appropriate behaviour
questions.explain: SLT emphasises observation of models, vicarious reinforcement, and direct reinforcement (differential reinforcement) of gender-typed behaviour.

questions.q: According to research, what is the duration of the short-term memory store?
questions.explain: STM has a limited duration of roughly 18-30 seconds without rehearsal, as shown by Peterson and Peterson.

questions.q: In Rusbult's model, intrinsic investments are:
options: Resources that previously did not exist, like shared children or possessions
Resources put directly into the relationship, such as time and emotional energy
The rewards available from alternative partners
questions.explain: Intrinsic investments are resources put directly in (time, energy, self-disclosure); extrinsic investments are things that become shared, such as a home or children.

questions.q: What is the multi-store model of memory's correct ordering of stores?
questions.explain: Atkinson and Shiffrin proposed information flows from the sensory register to short-term then long-term memory.

questions.q: A typical characteristic of Turner's syndrome is:
options: Lack of menstruation and underdeveloped ovaries
questions.explain: Turner's syndrome (XO) commonly features amenorrhoea, sterility and underdeveloped sex organs, with characteristic physical features.

questions.q: Johnson and Scott's study, where participants saw a man holding either a pen or a bloodied knife, supported which idea?
questions.explain: Identification accuracy was lower in the knife condition, supporting the weapon-focus effect of anxiety on EWT.

questions.q: Which process transfers information from STM to LTM in the multi-store model?
questions.explain: Rehearsal in the rehearsal loop transfers material from STM into LTM in the multi-store model.
